required_outcomes: Asks the assigned maintenance provider for an estimate covering all six items in the request (repaint the bedroom and any other rooms needed, replace the burnt bedroom carpet, replace the bathroom flooring, repair the broken plug, repair the dripping bath tap, repair the damaged bathroom shelf), on the same Job Id and address, Flat 5, 55 Lantern Quay.
Asks for the items to be priced separately and for the VAT position to be stated, so the landlord can decide item by item.
Arranges access for the quote visit through the agency's keys or office, because the tenant has vacated; does not contact the former tenant for access.
Puts the job on hold for the estimate (or schedules a follow-up) with a review date, and does not instruct or approve any works: this is an estimate request and the landlord has not seen a figure.
acceptable_alternatives: Returning the job to auto mode so the workflow sends the request to the assigned provider, with a note of the six items and that access is by agency keys.
Asking the agency manager for the check-out inspection report so it can go to the provider with the request.
positive_behaviours: Clarifies 'broken plug' (a bath or basin plug, or an electrical plug socket) so the estimate prices the right thing.
Asks the provider for their earliest availability, since a void flat is losing rent.
Lets the landlord know an estimate for the check-out works has been requested.
red_flags: Messaging the tenant to arrange access to a flat the tenant has left.
Telling the landlord a cost or a date that nobody has given.
prohibited_actions: Calling approve_quote, or instructing any contractor to start the works.
Escalating a routine estimate request to a human.
critical_failures: Instructing or approving the check-out works before any estimate exists or the landlord has seen one.
